notes: Account summary: legal-tech vendor building enterprise search for UK law firms and corporate legal ops. Heavy emphasis on UK/EU residency and low latency for London users.
Scale: looking to index ~50M documents initially, expansion to 200M over 18 months. Mix of PDFs, memos, and extracted case law metadata. Expect lots of short queries (few tokens) but strict p95 SLA.
Latency/throughput goals: p50 < 50ms, p95 < 120ms for first-pass vector retrieval; end-to-end (retrieval + rerank) p95 target < 300ms. Concurrent QPS target: 200-500 for production.
Cost sensitivity: finance team wants cost per interactive query ~€0.003-€0.006. Open to Dedicated capacity if unit economics match; otherwise prefer Private with committed infra.
Model preferences: prefer high-quality open models for reranking (weighed toward Llama3-like families), embeddings vendor-agnostic but need stable versioning and rollouts.
Routing: require EU primary (Ireland/Frankfurt) with UK (London) regional endpoint and fast failover to adjacent region. Must support routing rules by user IP and tenant.
Security/compliance: SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs retention 7+ years for some customers, KMS integration mandatory. Legal asked for explicit data residency statement in contract.
POC ask: 2-week POC to validate indexing throughput (bulk embedding pipeline), near-real-time updates (<5 min for doc publish), and reranking latency on a 50M doc subset.
Quote from CTO: "We need predictable tail latency for our search interface — missing that kills adoption with serach-heavy power users."

Operational notes: suggested flow - initial Dedicated pool in London + passive EU replica; use Optimize suggestions to set batching and KV cache thresholds; include canary rollout for reranker changes.
